pr_body:
For explicit (non-wildcard) names in expressions from requests with the `ignoreUnavailable` request option set to `true`, the Security filter removes names for "unavailable" resources. This behavior is theoretically correct, but in practice the cluster state might not be recovered at the point in time when the Security filter does the rewrite (this causes problems, see #90215); In any case, the logic to remove "unavailable" names is unnecessarily duplicated from Core's expression resolver.

This PR makes the expression resolver in the Security filter to NOT:

1) remove missing but authorized names (indices, aliases, datastreams)
2) remove authorized datastreams if context disallows datastreams
3) remove backing indices of authorized datastreams if context disallows datastreams

It will only remove names of unauthorized resources, and let the unavailable names go through to be handled (to be ignored or throw "not found" exception) by the expression resolver in Core.

Fixes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/90215
pr_title: Fix Security's expression resolver to not remove unavailable but authorized names
pr_comment: Hi @albertzaharovits, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

review_comment: Some EQL tests assert the audit log messages, and some will change because the transport request, which gets audited, is not rewritten anymore to erase authorized but unavailable indices.

Just to confirm that this is same to remove because core handles whether data stream is allowed in the context? Do we really need to remove it here? It does not seem to be strictly related to the original issue. It is also a bit inconsistent that `includeDataStreams` is still handled in the first lambda (the one backs `AuthorizedIndices.all`) but not here? Or should we also remove logic for `includeDataStreams` in the first lambda as well?
> Just to confirm that this is same to remove because core handles whether data stream is allowed in the context? 

Yes. In Core, accessing a datastream in a context that doesn't allow datastreams is handled similarly to a missing index, or to an alias when the request options ignore aliases.

> Do we really need to remove it here? It does not seem to be strictly related to the original issue. 
On the contrary, I think it would be inconsistent to continue to deal with non-authz unavailable conditions.

> It is also a bit inconsistent that includeDataStreams is still handled in the first lambda (the one backs AuthorizedIndices.all) but not here? Or should we also remove logic for includeDataStreams in the first lambda as well?

Yes, I agree it looks inconsistent. But I don't think we can get away from it. When expanding wildcards we need to know if to expand to datastreams and/or aliases too, but for explicit names we don't (and shouldn't).
We met today and also discussed this.
> It is also a bit inconsistent that includeDataStreams is still handled in the first lambda (the one backs AuthorizedIndices.all) but not here? Or should we also remove logic for includeDataStreams in the first lambda as well?

I think we're on the same page that it would be preferable to not check `includeDAtaStreams` when building the result of `AuthorizedIndices.all`. I think the code should work. But It's not obvious if it can affect performance. Therefore I prefer to keep this for a follow-up PR.

The `ignore_unavailable` request option does not currently work for "unavailable" aliases, see: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/844bb4cee573b4eb2b66fd2253d364ae7cf935fa/x-pack/plugin/security/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/security/authz/IndicesAndAliasesResolver.java#L375 .

It worked in this particular test by coincidence.
In this particular test the `test_1` index is authorized but non-existent, so the request was previously authorized after the request was rewritten to empty. But now this is not the case anymore.
`test_1` is authorized, so it is not considered "unavailable" from Security's POV,

From end-user's perspective, strictly speaking, this is a slight behaviour change:
* Status code from 404 to 403
* Response content from containing found aliases (and missing aliases) to unauthorized error response

Just want to call it out explicitly. But I don't think it is a real concern because the existing response is not a 200 anyway and it feels like an edge case.

Yes, it's indeed a behavior change for an edge case.

Rereading this now, after a week, I realise I haven't done a good job explaining what's going on here.
Let me try again:

The get aliases action in this test uses the "lenient expand open" request option, which means that missing explicit indices are ignored (and that wildcards can expand to empty).
The `test_1` index does not exist, and it is the only index in the request, so when retrieving the `non_authorized` alias for it, because of the request option, this previously returned a 200 empty result, because there were ultimately no indices to return the aliases for.
But, after the change, Security does not care if `test_1` exists or not (Core does, and if Security lets the request through, given the request option, it will return the empty result). For Security, the `test_1` is authorized, but the alias `non_authorized` is not, hence it will then return a 403 because of the alias. For **indices**, the request option `ignore_unavailable` silently discards unauthorized index names, but the option never discards unauthorized **aliases** (but maybe it should?).

Therefore, clients will notice behavior differences for this API, when **all** the indices are authorized but missing, the request option tells to ignore missing indices, and there are unauthorized aliases (missing or not). Before they got a 200 empty, after they get a 403.
They got

>  Before they got a 200 empty, after they get a 403.

Does it return 200 today? At REST layer, the response code is set to 404 if there is any explicitly requested alias not found.

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/c0e702c8365a068a8e0ff7290264e622158dea03/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/rest/action/admin/indices/RestGetAliasesAction.java#L130-L133

You're correct. It does return 404, in the existing code, with Security enabled, when user is only authorized for the `test_1` index that does not exist, but it is not authorized for the `non_authorized` alias.

This is an interesting point. The indexName `.ds-logs-foobar-*` contains a wildcard. I think this `check` will now return `true` here since the new name check should make it pass. It previously returns `false` because the name does not have an IndexAbstraction. If we believe the new behaviour is correct (returning `true`), should we retain this assertion but change it to `is(true)` and add a comment to say why it is the case? Just deleting it feels like we are leaving it unspecified and I don't think we want that.

IMO It doesn't make sense to test *patterns* at all for either `AuthorizedIndices#all` or `AuthorizedIndices#check`. In the main code it's only names of resources that are passed as arguments to these methods, never patterns. That's why I removed the test here. The assert can be `true` or `false` depending if the pattern in the request is greater than the the pattern in the permission, but it's not relevant.

> In the main code it's only names of resources that are passed as arguments to these methods, never patterns. 

I think it could happen when `expand_wildcards=none`? Not something we should optimize for. But the `check` should still work correctly for it.
